title: "svelte/no-useless-mustaches"

A mustache around a string literal adds nothing: the text can be written as it is. `--fix` writes the text, with `<` and `>` as `&lt;` and `&gt;`, and in an attribute with its quotes as `&quot;` or `&apos;`. It leaves a mustache with a comment, an escape sequence such as `\n`, a line break or white space at either end.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-useless-mustaches": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<p>{"Saved"}</p>
<img alt={'Logo'} src="/logo.svg" />
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<p>Saved</p>
<img alt="Logo" src="/logo.svg" />
```

## Options

| Option                  | Default | What it does                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ignoreIncludesComment` | `false` | Allow a mustache that has a comment in it                         |
| `ignoreStringEscape`    | `false` | Allow a string that has an escape sequence, such as `\n` or `\u00a0` |
